title: Supreme Court proposes sending Kolkata ward-map case to High Court bench, poll on hold
dek: The Chief Justice suggested staying the High Court's bar on the KMC election while a larger High Court bench decides the delimitation challenge. The parties respond on Monday, 30 November.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday proposed a way out of the legal deadlock over Kolkata's civic election, suggesting that it stay the Calcutta High Court order blocking the poll and move the challenge to the city's new ward map to a High Court division bench, with the election held off until that bench takes a view. The court gave the parties until Monday, 30 November, to respond, according to reports of the hearing.

The proposal came from a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, hearing the West Bengal government's appeal against the High Court's order of 6 November. The Chief Justice said the arrangement would put both sides on an "even keel" and stressed that it was "not an expression of opinion" on the merits, according to reports.

## What the court proposed

Under the proposal, the High Court's interim order, which bars the State Election Commission from notifying the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) poll on the redrawn wards, would be stayed. The writ petition challenging the delimitation, now pending before a single judge, would be transferred to a division bench. "Till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off," the Chief Justice said, according to reports.

In practice, that would leave the poll on hold for now but move the main challenge to a higher bench, which could speed up a final decision on whether the new map stands.

## What each side said

Senior advocate Bikas Ranjan Bhattacharya, appearing for Dipu Das, the former CPI(M) councillor who challenged the delimitation, initially agreed to the proposal, according to reports. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state government, asked for time to consult his clients.

Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for another respondent, also sought time to take instructions. He asked the court to avoid observations that could influence the division bench and said both sides should argue the case afresh there. "Please keep it neutral and we will have our day before the Division Bench," he said, according to reports. Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and his party had earlier filed a caveat in the Supreme Court asking to be heard before any order was passed.

## Background

The state's notification of 11 September raised the number of KMC wards from 144 to 209. Mr Das argues that the new map was drawn using electoral rolls rather than population figures and was designed to help the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party; the Trinamool also says the wards favour the BJP. The state says it was entitled to redraw the wards and that the challenge came too late. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has said that "those who are destined to lose the election go to court".

On 6 November a division bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee barred the poll from being notified on the revised wards until the challenge was decided. It questioned whether a state-appointed administrator could recommend ward changes under Section 601 of the KMC Act, 1980, a power it said lay with the elected corporation. The KMC, which serves about 45 lakh people, has had no elected board since June. The state filed its appeal in the Supreme Court on 13 November.

Howrah's new ward map faces a separate challenge. On Monday, Justice Raja Basu Chowdhury of the High Court declined to stay the Howrah Municipal Corporation poll schedule but said any announcement before the next hearing on 1 December would be subject to the court's later directions, according to reports.

## What happens next

The Supreme Court will hear the parties again on Monday, 30 November. If the state and the other respondents accept the proposal, the delimitation case will go to a High Court division bench and the KMC poll will wait for its decision. Polls to Kolkata, Howrah and five other civic bodies had been expected in the last week of December, according to earlier reports; that timetable now depends on how quickly the High Court rules.
